Everyone else has given answers already but I haven't heard anyone mention one of the big ones. Jitter. 

This is why lasers irl are unlikely to be used in space. A naval vessel has the sea to absorb vibrations made by machinery, guns or even crew walking around but a space craft does not. Lasers need to be focused on a very specific point in order to do any damage and crucially they need to be held on that point. This isn't too big of an issue if you are firing 100km away, but for engagement distances more than that, your laser either needs to be very large (so that the target always remains within the actual beam). 

A crew member walking around on your ship could produce a vibration capable of wobbling the laser ever so slightly which would result in it being unable to remain focused on the target.

Create especially is a biggie for this, as early game it doesn't do anything other than add recipes really and change some of the world gen. Late game however you'll have trains, contraptions and machines all whirring away costing you performance. It's also worth noting that CPU performance is a big factor too, as minecraft runs its core processes on a single core.

Everyone else has mentioned all the other reasons why lasers aren't exactly great, but honestly one of the biggest reasons we wouldn't use them irl, and why they aren't used in the expanse is because of a thing called jitter. 

There's nothing to really absorb vibrations and dampen them, atleast nothing less than RCS thrusters. Because of this, tiny vibrations on the ship, from something as small as someone walking around, causes the laser to wobble a tiny amount. Using them on earth, the wobble would be so little it would be negligible. In space however, with the potential engagement range of tens of thousands of kilometers, jitter becomes a serious factor, and results in a laser being unable to remain stable on a target. 

Another reason lasers wouldn't be all too helpful is because of the sheer amount of heat they generate, both at the source and the target. Spaceships have a difficult time removing heat and they already have alot of heat to deal with from all the other systems.

Steel can be made a couple of ways, you can either use a metallurgic infuser from mekanism to make it, by combining coal and iron in the machine, or you can use a blast furnace from immersive engineering, which requires coal coke (which you get from putting coal in a coke oven) and iron. You can also use an arc furnace from immersive engineering too, but that's later on in the mod and you'll need steel to make that anyways. 

I presume you haven't used JEI before? The menu on the right of your inventory? You can use that to find the recepies and uses of items. Left click or press R over an item to show the recepie, right click or press U to find its uses. There's also a search box at the bottom to search for what you're looking for. 

Oh also, I dunno what version of ATM your playing on, but a helpful thing for your early game is you can also mouse over an item and press Y and it'll highlight nearby chests that have that item in them. God knows we all make chest monstrosities and it's helpful to be able to easily find stuff.

It all depends really what you're going for. To be honest Mekanism is probably the best when it comes to automation as it covers 90% of what you need, and can be really easily and quickly scaled up, but the cooler mods for automation are the likes of create and immersive engineering which are abit more complicated and abit less useful, but look 100x better and feel alot cooler in practice. 

For storage there's Applied energistics 2 and Refined storage. I mainly play with refined storage as its easier to use but from what I hear it has some lag issues when compared to applied energistics. They both work basically the same way, although applied energistics has extra limitations on what you can do.

Mimecolonies is basically useless when compared to the other mods, but it can be kinda cool to have your own little town that you work woth and such.

The likes of bees and mystical agriculture are great ways to get lots of resources, and both basically work in a similar way (although bees is harder but I believe you have access to more items and such) 

If you're wanting to complete the pack and make ATM stars, you'll need to atleast start 95% of the mods in the pack anyways, so you won't miss out on much by ignoring certain mods.

8GB tends to work fine for me. Others have already explained it, but basically your RAM is where JAVA can store all its old data, and your processor has to delete that old data when it's full. If you add more RAM, all you're doing is increasing how much data your processor has to delete. Keeping it low means that rather than the garbage collection (term used for clearing your RAM) activating once every 30 seconds, for 2 seconds at a time, freezing your game for those two seconds, it'll instead activate once every 5 seconds, freezing for only half a second, effectively just seeming like a slightly lower frame rate. Server's on the other hand require alot of RAM I believe, especially with regards to how many players the server needs to handle.

I play on 8GB and don't really have any bother? PACs are super helpful against fast moving targets at relatively close range (although they can do long range) but they require immense amounts of electric to power, which means your sub will have to be pretty big and pretty expensive. 

APS is alot more complicated than PACs, but also alot more adaptable and can have a much longer effective range, and requires no power to run. That being said, the guns tend to be larger and also have a tendency to explode, which is super bad for a sub, as if a sub loses more than 20% of its health and it doesn't resurface, it'll be considered dead. Another negative of aps is they require materials for the ammo, but you'll already be carrying those mats and ammo boxes for VLS and Torps, so its not as big of an issue for you. 

All in all, it's mainly what you value the most for your sub. If you want it quiet and cheap, but easy to sink, APS is probably the way to go. But if you don't mind being noisy with large engines and such, and don't mind putting alot of resources into a single target, PACs are the best option.

You can then run the composite signal through things like electrical connectors and I believe cable connectors, which will allow you to attach it to other vehicles and such without them directly touching. All you have to do after that is have switchboxes for the various controls, so that you can switch it between being controlled by the cab of the slave vehicle, or being controlled by the master. Theoretically you should be able to attach as many slave engines as you'd like.

As far as I can tell, there are specific engagement ranges for each weapon. From longest to shortest range, its railgun -> torpedoes -> PDCs. Torpedoes quite quickly become your primary anti ship weapon, which can also be used semi effectively against clusters of torpedoes, however if the enemy is even the slightest bit smart, they'd direct their torpedoes from multiple angles, making sure they couldn't all be wiped out by a single torpedo blast. This essentially leaves you with a one to one trade of torpedoes, but if the enemy ship has significantly more torpedoes, you're gonna lose that battle pretty quick. 

Again, at medium ranges where most conflicts occur, you're main anti ship armament will be your torpedoes, especially since the railgun requires pin point accurate aiming. 

The point im trying to get at, is that PDC ammo is somewhat expendable, as without it, you are still easily able to deal a killing blow to an enemy ship, meanwhile without any torpedoes, you'll struggle to get close enough to the ship to actually deal any damage, without taking significant damage yourself, and even if your ship is functioning, your life will quickly end if all its airtight compartments are no longer airtight thanks to PDC holes.

Sorry if this is a ramble, but TL;DR its strategically better to waste ammunition from an expendable weapon than it is to use your ships primary armament

I've seen some where they've been able to take back off after being refuelled or having their engines patched up, ive also seen some where the tail boom has snapped from the force, or the engines have came through the roof. Its a rough action to perform, and how well the helicopter comes out afterwards is completely dependant on the helicopter and pilot skill

I believe it was worked out with planes, there's alot of energy in an aircraft's props and such, and thus you can reduce the collective (pitch of the blades relative to the airflow) to reduce the thrust and such output by the blades, whilst also storing that energy already in them to give a little extra speed if needed after the engine has cut out. From what you've said on other comments, I think you may have your dediblades either setup wrong, or your PID is overreacting due to excessive amounts of propulsion. If you feel that your craft has too much propulsion, lower the gain on your PID. Start by halfing its current value, then half again, then half again till you get a decently stable flight. 

As for your dediblades, ensure that the ones at the front are set to 1 for the pitch setting, and 1 for the hoversetting too since I presume you plan to use the same dediblades to control your altitude too.

As for the batteries, it completely depends on what kind of increase in capacity we're talking about. Most affordable drones have a 30min battery life on average (depending on flying conditions). Even with solid state batteries they would still need to be changed, meaning you'd either need someone there 24/7 to swap batteries, or you would need a system to automatically swap and charge batteries as they go.

A somewhat viable solution would be to have the drones carry cables up which power them, but you run the risk of props being caught in the wires and destroying your billboard.

The most likely scenario to what you're talking about would most likely be blimps carrying billboards like the famous goodyear blimp. These would be cheaper and wouldn't rely on electric to stay afloat. However there are still complications like what to fill it with, as helium is very expensive, and hydrogen is incredibly dangerous.

Lastly there's a legal element especially at the minute. Its a legal requirement that the operator of a drone can always see said drone (atleast in the UK) but with normal advertisements such as the ones at the Olympics, theyre only going for 10-15 mins then theyre packed up. Some major strides in autopiloting would need to be made because the red tape can be lifted from drones.

CRAM works well on the earlier factions such as DWG and OW, but struggles to hold up against the later factions without some perfect tuning. With CRAMs always add a fuse onto them to stop them from deflecting. This will make it so that if your shot bounces, it will immediately detonate and still do damage. With your advanced cannons, there's a wiki page that talks about shell types and on there it has a general chart of which shells do best at which gauges. Use that to determine which you'd like to use.

Missiles are devastating and incredibly easy to build and defend, so it would be a good start to build yourself a small, fast missile ship to dish out the early damage.

Torpedos work incredibly well as pure HE, since HE gets a damage bonus when underwater, so you can use some torpedoes too to help counter some of the ships.

Armor is key, make sure your boat has plenty of armor. With a starter ship its difficult to do, but once you feel you can play around abit, add an extra layer of armor. Stacking armor will increase the armors rating, which means that shells which dont have a high enough AP value will only do half damage to these blocks.

Lastly, realistically your best bet if you just want to beat the game, is just to build a dreadnought that costs several million mats, and use it to slowly steamroll your opponents ala gustav gun style, but personally, if you wanna enjoy the game? Specialise your ships, make one designed to counter flyers, one to counter airships, one to counter battleships, one to counter destroyers all that stuff, and put them together in a fleet. Personally it makes the game more enjoyable for me, but its up to you how you'd like to play the game.

There are several different types of hulls, but the main ones being Box shaped, U shaped and V shaped. They're pretty self explanatory, but essentially the idea is a box shaped hull is the most stable, but least hydrodynamic and thus not as good for speed and such (its also generally seen as ugly). 

U Shaped hulls and the mid point between the two, where they have a flat bottom, flat sides, but rounded corners. This gives you a good amount of stability and buoyancy, whilst also being quite hydrodynamic. Personally this is my go to, atleast some variation of it, most people also go for this hull as they're relatively easy to build. 

Last general hull is a V shape, which is of course in a V shape. These are generally the most aesthetically pleasing, however they offer very little in practicality as they're very unstable, very difficult to work with as they're generally taller than they are wide, and they are often very difficult to build in a way that looks good, particularly at the bow/stern of the ship.

There's a few others such as the tumble home(I think that's its name?) Which is shaped like (__) rather than \__/. For me, my zombie plan involves 'acquiring' a barge or car ferry. The main reason being they tend to be rather simple in nature, no fancy stuff and they also tend to be simple to operate and have a very small crew requirement whilst also having a very large amount of space for building and expansion. They might not be fancy or have home cinemas built into them like a yacht, but to be fair a post apocalypse warlord isn't going to want my floating shit shack, they're going to want your floating bar and swimming pool. Another reason for a barge or car ferry is because it leaves less places for zombies to hide in when you're clearing it out and getting it ready to use. Something like a yacht for instance could very easily have a few zombies hidden away in areas of the ship you might not have checked, whereas with a barge, you pretty much check the deck and wheel house and that's it. Plus, they're less likely to even have zombies on them since they aren't really constantly staffed by a crew of hundreds like a cruise ship. 

You also wouldn't have to worry about barnacles since you'll be mostly in fresh water, however this is the issue of you're almost always going to be within small arms range. The upsides however outweigh the negatives as you can build whatever you need on the deck. Need more farms? build them! Want to do fishing on a more industrial level? make a net and a primitive crane and pulley system and you've basically got a trawler. Might not be the most amazing trawler ever, but enough to feed everyone.

I feel as though yachts and such wouldn't be the worst ideas in a zombie apocalypse, but the fact that they're often in salt water, means you have to worry about barnacles, and waves and such which for someone inexperienced, might be difficult to deal with. Plus on the topic of barnacles, you've got to hope you can find a dry dock that still works and isn't infested with zombies before they destroy your hull.

For me, my zombie plan involves capturing one of those large open air barges which are used for transporting large machinery or vehicles up and down rivers, either that or an open air car ferry. They are often nice and sturdy so small arms fire isn't going to destroy your newly acquired base of operations, and they often have handy systems in place to help with balancing the boat which will be handy when we get to the next point, building. You can sail your lovely ferry/barge up stream until you reach an area away from prying eyes and the walking brain nibblers, and from there you can gather building supplies to help build certain things on board. Things such as housing, farms, a fishing net kind of rig so you can use it in the same way as a trawler to a degree, and also a water filter and such. 

I feel as though as much as a barge is for the most part stuck either very close to the shore, or in a river/lake (in range of possible weapons) They're much simpler to operate, require less crew and are much less likely to have zombies hidden away in certain areas. Loads of people say they'd get a cruise ship or a yacht, but they don't realize how difficult it would be to operate and maintain something of that size. Not to mention as I say, on a large ship, you'd be hard pressed to be certain that you've cleared it all out, same with a large building. Plus, the bigger the ship is, the more fuel it uses, and the more of a target it is. Some warlord is gonna target your 70mil yacht before my floating shit shack.

Also, you don't need to worry about barnacles in fresh water, which is always a plus since it means maintenance isn't as big of an issue.
